title: Untitled (Memory is your image of perfection) [Postcard]

description.main: A Fotofolio postcard of Barbara Kruger's Untitled (Memory is your image of perfection), 1982, which sets its phrase down an X-ray of a full human skeleton.
description.extended:
A Fotofolio postcard of Barbara Kruger's Untitled (Memory is your image of perfection), 1982, which sets its phrase down an X-ray of a full human skeleton.

The card reproduces the image in color at 15 by 11 cm, inside a red border. The sentence is broken into four bands placed down the length of the body, from the chest to the feet. The source work is a photograph, 155 by 86 cm, in the collection of the Museum of Contemporary Art San Diego. The National Gallery of Art in Washington borrowed it for In the Tower: Barbara Kruger, which ran from September 2016 to January 2017.
description.artist_bio: Barbara Kruger (b. 1945, Newark) is an American conceptual artist associated with the Pictures Generation. After working as a designer and picture editor at Conde Nast magazines, she began in the late 1970s to pair found black-and-white photographs with declarative text in Futura Bold Oblique, white on red. The Barbara Kruger Catalogue Raisonne (barbarakruger.org) documents the work; she is represented by Sprueth Magers and David Zwirner.
